item.content:encoded:
Theater-level is strategic, operation-level is tactical. Part of the reason I went with 5 MT was to make implications as to where the Foundation sees that distinction. That yield is reserved for real-world MAD and city-killing1, but was deployed here as a tactical failsafe for Operation Harmonizer; the sole objective of which was the elimination of 333-C 'DISCORD' from 333-B, the City, and consequentially, 333-A, the Song, by any possible means.

To address a criticism raised above, I would argue very strongly against the nuke or its yield being excessive - or for that matter, that the Foundation doesn't have 5 MT backpack nukes. The story between the lines is the Foundation eyeing an endgame and going all-in. To that end, there is no overkill. I erred on the side of understatement in most areas save the device's yield; I hoped it would push people to consider what could warrant that, and consider the implications of the last addendum. I feel to simply state them or make it more explicit would cheapen the whole thing, and that even this is saying too much.

Footnotes
1. Which, like, come on now.

That Operation wasn't so much a test as an attempt to secure the city by force because of its potential value. The nuke was on standby as a panic button. Detonation of the nuke would likely have killed the performers keeping the city up, meaning to check, the score would need to be performed again. So doing would manifest another instance of the entity, making the actual efficacy of the nuke a metaphysical consideration. At least, that's how I thought of it. As far as the Foundation would be concerned, they'd simply see the entity as unaffected the next time the score was played.

You do raise a good point, though. I'll see about cutting the nuke and taking another approach. Thanks for the feedback.
